provider: ElevenLabs voice library, via the ElevenLabs connector

steve.display: Steve Mercer (also voices his copy Stephen)
steve.why: A calm, articulate, soft-spoken character voice with a precise edge that fits Steve's engineer reasoning and dry delivery.

nora.display: Nora Reyes (also voices her copy Iris)
nora.why: Closest match to the voice Ward had before: about 197 Hz against 184 Hz, with a similar pitch range and brightness. You liked that voice for Nora.

archivist.display: The Archivist (also her shore echo, Mrs. Penhallow)
archivist.why: A wise, quietly luminous oracle tone that gives her 900 years of weight and still sounds kind.

helen.why: A smart, natural senior who sounds like she has lived a full life, so Helen comes across as an ordinary, grounded mom.

calder.why: Commanding and crisp, a good pick if Calder should sound more like the law and less like a neighbor when she pushes back on federal agents.

dale.display: Dale Kittredge (also Pell, his Veyri copy)
dale.why: Blue-collar, believably gruff tradesman voice that fits a real postal worker and has enough warmth to push into Pell's eagerness.

agnes.display: Agnes Penhallow (echo; also plays the original Agnes)
agnes.why: Crisp diction with a light theatrical lilt, a good match for the riddling, slightly uncanny echo and the grammar-correcting teacher.

saren.why: Polite and educational with a posh-villain option, close to a courteous official who never shouts.

wen.why: Deep, composed, Chinese-accented and mature, fitting a senior scientist who guards a secret with quiet confidence.

shaw.why: Raspy with sarcastic undertones, ideal for Shaw's barbs at officials and at Wen.

rook.display: Special Agent Adrian Rook (copy; also plays the real Rook)
rook.why: Husky, brooding and emotive, the more worn-down option that suits the tired real Rook and the copy's fear-driven betrayal.

frank.why: A friendly, comforting older American voice that holds up well for radio-log lines like his K7BLW calls.

ward.why: Warm, authoritative and polished like a broadcast, a natural fit for a national address.

operator.why: Clear, warm voice of a man in his 70s, close in age to Frank's club friends.

autorick.why: Built for radio station automation, which is literally what AutoRick is; upbeat and generic in a way that suits a corporate replacement host.

choir.why: A regal, mythic, ethereal tone for a lighter, more choral-sounding Choir that layers well with effects.

carmen.details: female · middle_aged · Latin American in English
carmen.why: An English voice with a natural Latin accent and an outgoing, talkative energy for the side of Carmen that runs the dinner table.

gus.voice_name: Kelvin Southern Cheerful Call Center Voice
gus.why: A soft, cheerful, mildly funny American tenor for a small-town shopkeeper Gus with no accent. It fits "Good evening. May I help you?"

lyle.why: An easygoing, resonant middle-aged American voice with enough polish to also sound like the well-behaved copy.

general_cn.details: male · Chinese-influenced English with a light British tone
general_cn.why: Calm and confident with formally learned English, which fits a general trained in diplomatic English.

tomas.why: A young Mexican-American reviewer voice that already sounds like someone talking to an online audience.

luis.details: male · middle_aged · Northern Mexican in English
luis.why: A real Mexican man speaking English with a northern Mexican accent, the most authentic accent match here, though he sounds a little younger than 67.

general_us.why: An older, gravelly voice with weight and restraint that fits a veteran general weighing every word.

mateo.details: male · middle_aged · American with slight Mexican accent
mateo.why: A middle-aged Latino man with a slight Mexican accent, right for a US-raised son of Mexican immigrant parents.

rafa.why: A low, smooth, personable US-born Latino voice for a softer, more introverted Rafa.

guard.why: Eager to assist and slightly unreal, which is exactly how an alien attendant offering hold music should land.

confirmed.by: user, after listening to every voice sample
confirmed.checks: All 26 voice IDs exist; 24 shared library voices and 2 premade voices; every voice is verified for eleven_v4; each sample matches the clip heard during casting.

before_recording: Add the 24 shared library voices to the ElevenLabs account (24 of the 29 free voice slots on the Creator plan). Premade Bill and Roger need no slot.
Record soon after adding: Christine (Wen) has a 30-day creator notice period, Carol (Helen) 90 days, Luis (Luis Reyes) and Sebastian (Rafa) 180 days.
Use model eleven_v4 for every line, including narration, and record each copy with its original's voice.
